title: From Approval to Execution: Reconstruction-Aware Repair Analysis for LLM-Agent Software
abstract: arXiv:2609.26529v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Approval mechanisms have become a primary safeguard for consequential actions in LLM-agent software. Yet the action shown for approval is often not the object ultimately consumed: workflow reload, transcript projection, argument rebinding, and durable-state lookup may reconstruct it before execution. Existing fieldflow and check-coverage analyses can establish that expected fields were inspected, but not that the inspected object version reaches the sink or that no replacement intervenes between check and use. Consequently, a locally complete repair may still leave a residual authorization bypass after reconstruction. We address this problem through three designs. (1) We formulate reconstruction-stable authorization (ReSA) over representation transitions, sink dependencies, consumed versions, and grant scope. (2) We derive obligations that judge candidate repairs and expose residual sink suffixes. (3) We implement the analysis in APAS-Fi

translated_title: 从批准到执行：面向LLM智能体软件的重构感知修复分析
translated_abstract: 批准机制已成为LLM智能体软件中对重大操作进行防护的首要安全保障。然而，用于审批展示的操作往往并非最终被消费的对象：工作流重载、对话记录投影、参数重绑定以及持久状态查找都可能在执行前对该对象进行重构。现有的字段流与检查覆盖分析能够证明预期字段已被检查，但无法证明被检查的对象版本确实到达了汇点，也无法证明在检查与使用之间没有发生替换。因此，一个局部完备的修复在重构之后仍可能留下残留的授权绕过漏洞。我们通过三项设计来解决这一问题：（1）我们在表示转换、汇点依赖、被消费版本与授权范围之上形式化了重构稳定授权；（2）我们推导出用于判定候选修复并暴露残留汇点后缀的义务；（3）我们在APAS-Fi中实现了该分析。
tldr: 该论文提出重构稳定授权的形式化框架ReSA及相应的修复判定义务，用于发现并消除LLM智能体软件中因执行前对象重构而产生的残留授权绕过漏洞。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a formalization of reconstruction-stable authorization (ReSA) along with repair-judgment obligations to detect and eliminate residual authorization bypasses caused by object reconstruction before execution in LLM-agent software.
